title: Chelsea have 'no chance of achieving anything' with Colwill and Fofana, claims Carragher
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutChelsea have 'no chance of achieving anything' with Colwill and Fofana, claims CarragherShareChelsea have struggled defensively this season, and Jamie Carragher believes the Blues must sign a new centre-back as soon as possible.Jamie Carragher believes Chelsea have "absolutely no chance of achieving anything" with the centre-back partnership of Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana.
Chelsea's poor form in 2026-27 continued after the international break following a 4-1 home defeat to Leeds United on Saturday.
The Blues lost by 3+ goals while conceding 4+ goals at home in the Premier League for just the fourth time, last doing so against Brentford in April 2022 (also 4-1).

It also marked Xabi Alonso's joint-biggest losing margin at home to any side as a manager (also 0-3 v Porto with Bayer Leverkusen in the 2022-23 Champions League), while it was the Blues' 100th home defeat in the Premier League (658th home match).

Chelsea are eighth in the English top-flight after 11 games, and only Crystal Palace (27), Manchester United (23), Ipswich Town (22) and Coventry City (21) have conceded more goals in the competition this term than Alonso's side (20).
With summer signing Maxence Lacroix out injured, Colwill and Fofana started against Leeds, but Carragher insisted Chelsea must buy a new centre-back in January.

"Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don't change it in January, they're going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League," Carragher said on Sky Sports.

"Colwill at Sunderland against [Brian] Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time. Fofana's performance against Manchester United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you'll see from a centre-back this season.

"As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there. It almost feels like you've got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well.
"This is not going to change with what they have. Lacroix is a decent player, that's a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season.
"Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they've got absolutely no chance of achieving anything."
